s50l:S1Q04F.q: How would you reduce the sorting cost for millions of customers while preserving the tie rule?
s50l:S1Q04F.label: gemini-3.5-flash-lite_fturn-s50l-B
s50l:S1Q04F.spoken: I'd avoid a full sort by using a min-heap or Quickselect to pull the top k items in O(N log k) time instead of O(N log N). To keep the tie rule intact, I use a composite key of the score and the negated row index, which lets the selection algorithm break ties deterministically by original order.
s50l:S1Q04F.raw: I'd avoid a full sort by using a min-heap or Quickselect to pull the top $k$ items in $O(N \log k)$ time instead of $O(N \log N)$. To keep the tie rule intact, I use a composite key of the score and the negated row index, which lets the selection algorithm break ties deterministically by original order.

s50l:S1Q06F.q: How would you index those tables, and what changes if historical records can be corrected after ingestion?
s50l:S1Q06F.label: gemini-3.5-flash-lite_fturn-s50l-B
s50l:S1Q06F.spoken: For indexing, I'd build a composite index on the events table covering customer ID, event time, and ingested at, alongside a primary key on snapshots. If historical records can be corrected, I'd switch to a temporal or event-sourced pattern, tracking transaction time separately from valid time so our point-in-time views stay deterministic.

s50l:S2Q05F.q: An example where that greedy policy gives poor coverage, and tell me how you would incorporate redundancy or multi hop dependencies.
s50l:S2Q05F.label: gemini-3.5-flash-lite_fturn-s50l-B
s50l:S2Q05F.spoken: A greedy relevance approach fails when top chunks cluster in the same document section, starving the context of necessary background. To fix that, I apply Maximal Marginal Relevance to enforce diversity and reduce redundancy. For multi-hop dependencies, I use agentic query decomposition to pull supporting evidence step-by-step before finalizing the context budget.

s50l:S2Q08F.q: How do you prove the replacement index is sufficiently complete and current before you send production traffic to it?
s50l:S2Q08F.label: gemini-3.5-flash-lite_fturn-s50l-B
s50l:S2Q08F.spoken: I validate completeness by running a direct count-parity check against our PostgreSQL source of truth to ensure zero documents were missed during the backfill. For currency, I run the new index in shadow mode alongside the legacy one, using our golden evaluation set and automated LLM-as-judge checks to confirm retrieval parity before cutting over production traffic.

s50l:D1.q: How would you index those tables, and what changes if historical records can be corrected after ingestion?
s50l:D1.label: gemini-3.5-flash-lite_fturn-s50l-B
s50l:D1.spoken: I’d index those tables on a composite key of customer ID and timestamp for efficient time-series lookups, plus a unique index on the record ID. If historical records can be corrected, I'd implement a bitemporal model tracking both valid time and transaction time. That ensures corrections update ingestion views without breaking reproducibility for past audit snapshots.

s50l:D2.q: An example where that greedy policy gives poor coverage, and tell me how you would incorporate redundancy or multi hop dependencies.
s50l:D2.label: gemini-3.5-flash-lite_fturn-s50l-B
s50l:D2.spoken: Imagine a query comparing two distinct security clauses in a compliance audit; a greedy relevance matcher might pull the top three chunks from section one because they score highest on keyword overlap, completely missing section two. To incorporate redundancy, I apply Maximal Marginal Relevance scoring to penalize semantic duplication and force diversity into the context window. For multi-hop dependencies, I implement an agentic decomposition loop where the output of the first retrieval hop dynamically generates the search filters or query parameters for the next step.

s50l:D3.q: How do you prove the replacement index is sufficiently complete and current before you send production traffic to it?
s50l:D3.label: gemini-3.5-flash-lite_fturn-s50l-B
s50l:D3.spoken: I run a dual-write pipeline to shadow the new index, then evaluate its retrieval metrics against our gold dataset to guarantee recall matches or exceeds production. For currency, I audit document counts against our source of truth and verify the latest sync timestamp sits within our freshness SLA before executing a blue-green traffic switch.
